problem: Prior dialog-based navigation tasks (CVDN, HANNA, DialFRED, TEACh) assume an omniscient guide who knows the navigator's exact location, so vague questions like 'help' still get perfect answers and dialog quality is not truly tested; evaluation also often ignores the dialog itself.
motivation: Real-world help-seeking (e.g. a lost person calling a friend) requires the helper to infer where the asker is. A remote, non-omniscient guide forces the navigator to ask informative, grounded questions and the guide to localize before answering. Studying this needs a dataset of human-human dialog with trajectories and a holistic benchmark covering all subtasks.
key_idea: Introduce DialNav, a cooperative navigation task where a navigator and a remote guide (who knows the house but not the navigator's location) converse over multiple turns, along with the RAIN human-human dataset and a modular holistic benchmark.
insight: Dialog helps in seen environments (SR 18.2 -> 27.0) but not in unseen ones (val unseen SR 15.4 -> 13.9, test 12.7 -> 11.9), because small data and cascading error across question generation, localization and answer generation hurt. Giving the guide ground-truth location improves SR on every split (e.g. val unseen 13.9 -> 19.8), so localization and question quality are bottlenecks. Removing pretraining from the navigation module (SR 27.0 -> 9.2) or the answer generation module (SR 27.0 -> 11.7) hurts most, while LLaVA/Llama generate more fluent QA but LANA is better grounded.
method: Task/episode definition: episode E=(G,b,R,I,T,D) on Matterport3D nav graphs; the navigator starts from an ambiguous hint ('The goal room contains X'), the guide knows the house and goal but not the navigator's location, and the dialog is unlimited alternating turns.

RAIN data collection: a web tool with a navigator interface (chat, guess button) and a guide interface (house layout, room list, shortest path from a selected node); 2,231 episodes (1,559 train, 111 val seen, 276 val unseen, 285 test), 1.87 QA pairs per episode on average, ~USD 7,500.
Navigator navigation module: DUET (best; pretrained on ScaleVLN), treating the accumulated dialog as one instruction; HAMT compared.
Whether-to-ask: Fixed-Interval, Confidence Thresholding, and a learned Decision Head on DUET features (baseline), which trade off SR against dialog turn count.
Question generation: LANA (pretrained as an instruction generator, finetuned on RAIN) describes the current panorama; LLaVA-1.5 prompted as an alternative.
Guide localization: SCN or GCN ranking models from the LED task (WAY-pretrained, finetuned on RAIN) predict the navigator's node from the question; GCN is the baseline.
Answer generation: LANA finetuned to describe the path from the estimated location to the goal (baseline); Llama-3.1-8B prompted with LLaVA captions of the path as an alternative.
Holistic cooperative evaluation: SR, OSR, SPL, NE plus NSC (steps), DTC (dialog turns), LE (localization error); averaged over 5 runs.

setting.backbone: DUET (ScaleVLN-pretrained) navigator + Decision Head, LANA for question/answer generation, GCN localizer (all finetuned on RAIN); LLaVA-1.5 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as prompted alternatives
setting.model_size: LLaVA-1.5 7B and Llama-3.1 8B for the alternatives; modules otherwise small
setting.training_data: RAIN (1,559 train episodes, 4,493 segment instances) plus pretraining: ScaleVLN for navigation, VLN instruction generation for LANA, WAY dataset for localization
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views at nav-graph nodes plus dialog text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints, plus ask-question/stop decisions
setting.privileged: none for the main setup (guide uses the house map but not the navigator location); the '+GT Loc.' ablation gives the guide the navigator's ground-truth location

results: With dialog, val-seen SR rises from 18.2 to 27.0 (SPL 17.3 to 25.4), but in unseen environments dialog does not help (val unseen SR 13.9 vs 15.4 without; test 11.9 vs 12.7), though it cuts excessive exploration (NSC). Ground-truth localization gives the best SR on every split (19.8 val unseen, 17.3 test), showing error propagation from question generation and localization.
limitations: Small, costly dataset (2,231 episodes) leads to poor generalization to unseen houses; baseline SR is ~12-14% there.
Modular pipeline with cascading errors; the guide/navigator modules use simplified inputs (only the last question for localization, only remaining path for answers), and LANA output is disfluent.
Evaluation is non-deterministic and offline annotations become invalid under predicted dialog; no end-to-end model.
